newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries up marginally in London, seen confined.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries up marginally in London, seen confined.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices inched up slightly in London trade on Friday and traders said they were likely to finish the week on a stable note with an approaching options expiry keeping the market in check.

"We tried to break up last night and it came back in the range," said a dealer at a European bank in London. "This afternoon you've got the option expiry. I really don't see too much that's going to move it."
May T-bond options are due to expire at 1700 GMT
The trader said that with open interest focused on 108-00 calls or 106-00 puts, the market was likely to stay near the 108-00 level.
June T-bond futures at 1000 GMT were at 107-30, up 3/32 from the prior Chicago finish.

In the cash market, the benchmark long bond was at 94-16,20, for a yield of 7.07 percent, compared with 94-15,16 at the Tokyo finish and 94-17,18 in New York. Along with the options expiry, the market was looking ahead to the University of Michigan sentiment survey for April due at 1400 GMT. Economists forecast it to give a reading of 99.8, down slightly from 100.0 perviously.
Economists said that while Treasuries look a little sturdier than in recent weeks, there was still a sense of apprehension about debt markets overall.

"The U.S. market has rebounded and that seems to be helping," said Mark Fox, chief Europpean strategist for fixed income at Lehman Brothers in London. But he added, "If the U.S. has another big selloff no other market can resist that."
Fox said the big debate in the debt markets was how to play the U.S./European spreads. He said many have been overweight Europe and underweight the U.S.
"Our view is that around these levels you should move back into the U.S.," he said.
The spread between 10-year U.S. and German cash yields was at 114 basis points at 1040 GMT.
